proof_audit.topic: Nonlinear claims and nonduplicated loss attribution
proof_audit.audit: The bond and borrower claim have explicit future cash dates and positive discount factors. Differentiation gives negative duration and positive bond convexity. The joint loan mark includes the rate-credit interaction exactly; rate-first plus credit-at-new-yield is an identity. Mark loss, a later receipt or sale at that mark, principal paydown and deposit withdrawal are distinguished transaction by transaction. Tomorrow's interest is reported separately from the current-instant accounting convention.

Common total obligation, fixed pari passu shares, limited liability, external cash, no other realizable resources and simultaneous enforceable batch settlement are specified. For interbank share a<1 the min map is a self-map of the compact square and is a contraction in maximum norm. A geometric Cauchy bound proves existence and continuity yields a fixed point; the contraction inequality proves uniqueness. Every solution is in one of four capped/uncapped regimes. Candidate labels can coincide at a boundary without creating multiple payment vectors. The a=1 closed-cycle counterexample explicitly limits the result.

proof_audit.topic: Network resource conservation, monotonicity and continuity
proof_audit.audit: Retained balances are nonnegative; summing them cancels internal transfers and yields external cash equal to outside payments plus retained cash. Monotone iterations from zero prove payments cannot decrease when external cash increases. The fixed-point perturbation bound 1/(1-a) proves continuity in external cash. The loss transmitted through the second node is already included in I's final mark and is not a separate added impairment.

Old and new collateral use disjoint inventory fractions. The old pool stays reserved even after principal paydown, so there is no collateral recycling. A minimum planned draw targets the cash floor but is capped by both the actually available facility and free collateral. Actual payments follow a specified old-creditor-then-depositor priority; each is limited to remaining cash and unpaid amounts stay in the liability. The signed full-payment budget is a feasibility certificate, not an executed negative cash balance. Every current journal balances independently calculated equity. Later principal and interest cannot be financed by simply pointing to one- and two-year receipts.

For a fixed scenario, each component loss is bounded by its menu maximum; summing and taking a maximum proves max(sum)<=sum(max). Gains remain in the totals. The supplied menu has incompatible component extrema and an exact positive gap; no independence or confidence level is asserted. Contract identifiers, institution versus consolidated perimeter and the common industrial/rate factors explain why nominal debtor counts do not prove diversification.

The supported severity set is the compact interval [0,1], with nonnegative driver slopes and endpoint domain tests. Asset marks, network receipts and collateral capacity are continuous/nonincreasing; losses, required paydown and requests are nondecreasing. Both slacks and their minimum are continuous/nonincreasing. The closed trigger set is either empty, contains zero, or has an attained first boundary. Bisection preserves a strictly safe lower endpoint and a weakly triggering upper endpoint with exact width 2^-n, even under plateaus. Capacity uses maximum available drawing, not the minimum-draw policy's chosen closing cash. Strict positive shortage is explicitly distinguished from the zero-cash infimum. The one-dimensional family does not contain the separately tested operational outage.

remaining_limits: Scenarios are conditional synthetic assumptions without calibrated probabilities, empirical plausibility certification or a missing-tail guarantee.

The clearing proof requires the specified simultaneous batch, pari passu shares, no extra resources/default costs and a<1. It does not solve arbitrary financial networks or gross-settlement liquidity.
The stress equity convention marks assets against par principal liabilities; it is not a complete fair-value account, regulatory ratio or statutory accounting implementation.

Current cutoff execution does not prove next-day refinancing, legal enforceability, future asset-sale prices or survival to asset maturity. Prices and haircuts remain exogenous; fire-sale endogeneity needs a new explicit mechanism.
The reverse minimum covers only the supported one-dimensional monotone family and closed intervention thresholds, not the weakest conceivable route to strict default.
Separate peer/coordinator acceptance, dependency acceptance, shared reader/offline/UI checks and publication remain pending.
